en: Cherry blossoms, cherry blossoms! The sky of Yayoi, as far as the eye can see:
is it mist, or is it cloud? A fragrance comes forth. Come now, come now,
rom: Sakura, sakura, Yayoi no sora wa, miwatasu kagiri,
kasumi ka kumo ka, nioi zo izuru. Iza ya, iza ya,
notes: Romanization: modified Hepburn of the words as they are read and sung (modern pronunciation); the historical kana spelling of the original is not transliterated letter by letter (にほひ nioi, いづる izuru, ゆかむ yukan). If the editor wants the written kana instead: nihohi, idzuru, yukamu. 櫻 and 彌生 are old character forms (桜, 弥生), read sakura, Yayoi. 〳〵 is the repeat sign for いざや, written out (iza ya, iza ya). The 。 phrase marks become commas, with a full stop where the sense ends.
The import's line division is kept: three phrases on each of the first two lines, the last phrase alone.
line 1: Yayoi, the third month of the old lunar calendar (roughly April), kept as a name.
line 2: 'mist or cloud' are the masses of blossom seen from afar (implied, not said).
line 2: 'nioi' in classical Japanese is a fragrance but also a glowing colour or beauty; 'a fragrance comes forth' keeps the commoner reading, with the visual sense possible.
line 2: 'iza ya', 'come now', an urging call.
